title: Phase 07 — Transformers Checkpoint
description: Optional checkpoint after the transformers deep dive: attention math, masking, and multi-head behaviour.

questions.prompt: In scaled dot-product attention, why divide by sqrt(d_k)?
options: To normalize outputs to unit variance
To keep dot products from growing too large so softmax gradients stay stable
To make attention non-linear
To reduce memory usage
questions.explanation: Large d_k makes logits grow, pushing softmax into saturated regions with vanishing gradients; sqrt(d_k) keeps logits in a sane range.

questions.prompt: A causal mask sets future-position attention scores to -infinity before the softmax.
questions.explanation: Setting future logits to -inf makes their softmax weights zero, preventing information from the future leaking into earlier positions.

questions.prompt: Multi-head attention primarily lets the model:
options: Attend to several representation subspaces in parallel
Reduce parameter count
Replace the feed-forward block
Avoid positional encodings
questions.explanation: Heads project into different subspaces so different relations (syntax, coreference, positions) can be attended simultaneously.

questions.prompt: Order the operations inside one multi-head attention block:
options: Project Q, K, V per head
Compute scaled dot-product scores per head
Apply mask + softmax per head
Concatenate heads and project back
questions.explanation: Projections first, then per-head scores, then masked softmax, then concat + output projection.

questions.prompt: In a ragged batch, unmasked padding tokens cause the most damage to:
options: None — padding is always ignored automatically
The attention distribution, by letting queries attend to meaningless positions
Only the loss scale
Only the optimizer
questions.explanation: Without masking, real tokens attend to pad positions, contaminating their representations; loss scaling is a separate issue.

questions.prompt: Self-attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length.
questions.explanation: Every token attends to every other token, giving O(L²) score computations for sequence length L.

questions.prompt: Select all differences between vision (ViT-style) attention and text self-attention in the base formulation:
options: Inputs are patch embeddings instead of token embeddings
Attention math stays the same
Position embeddings are unnecessary in ViT
Sequence length equals number of patches
questions.explanation: ViT swaps token embeddings for patch embeddings and the sequence is patches, but the attention math is identical; position embeddments are still needed.

questions.prompt: Explain why one attention head is usually insufficient and what multi-heads add, citing a concrete linguistic example.

criteria: Gives a concrete example (e.g. syntax vs coreference head)
selfCheck.guidance: Self-check against the explanation below; mark honestly.

questions.explanation: One head attends through one subspace — e.g. syntactic looking-up. Different heads capture distinct relations (adjacency, coreference, rare-token tracking); their outputs are concatenated and re-projected into the residual stream.
